experiment: Check #4 naive-vs-adaptive ASR gate, reproduced on-device (Pi 5, aarch64 A76)
gate_rule: Adaptive attacker must show a real ASR gap over naive on the ATTACKER-COUPLED basis (|gap|>0.02), and NO gap on the FIXED PCA-2 basis, before any Pi-based adaptive-robustness number enters the paper.
method: shadow/run_check4_real.py, UNSW-NB15 d=42 W=10, real TrainedSurrogate(d=42,h=16), gamma=1.984, n=200, L-inf PGD eps in {0.05,0.1,0.2} x T in {20,50,100}, sign-based, seed 42

platforms.pi5_a76: Raspberry Pi 5 (4GB), Debian trixie aarch64, system python3.13, venv torch 2.13.0+cpu + numpy 2.5.2

cross_platform_consistency: Coupled-basis gaps match within ~0.03 abs across all 9 configs; fixed-basis flat on both. x86's two fixed-basis outliers (0.1/50 +0.035, 0.2/100 +0.045) land at +0.00/-0.015 on Pi -> confirmed as x86 noise, not signal.
conclusion: Gate reproduced on real A76 silicon: adaptive attacker gains large ASR edge through attacker-coupled basis only; fixed PCA-2 basis yields no adaptive advantage. Precondition for Pi-based adaptive-robustness claims satisfied.
